links.reason: 2555 is the city's reported question (தவஞ் செய்யா திகழ்ந்திருப்ப தென்பார்); 3016 only says துறவு is மாண்பு for a king, so it is a loose answer, not a fulfilment, and 3016's sense is flagged uncertain.

471 lists bathing, sandal, garland and food; nothing in it speaks of the host's face (முகனமர்ந்து) that Kural 84 turns on, so 'welcome is a trained skill' and 'women set aside their looks' are not in the Tamil.

Both give the flesh-eaters molten metal in the mouth: 1934 'செப்புத் திரள் வாயைப் பிளந்து மடுப்பார்' and 2768 'உருக வெந்த பாளத்தை... வாய் புகுத்தல்'; the 'look at these' mockery in 1934 and 'வருக' in 2768 are true, so the fixed Jain punishment is shown across two books.

1915 has Vijayai say 'யான் அலன் ஔவை; ஆவாள் சுநந்தையே... தந்தை கந்துக்கடன்', which fulfils the foster bond 473 shows in 'தாயுயர் மிக்க தந்தை'; the note is accurate and the ratification by the birth mother is more than plot order.

528 has the king say the Vidyadhara wealth is the fruit of former austerity (மேலை விழுத்தவம்); Naladiyar 265 says the wealth of the unjust is 'வினைப்பயன்'. The 'rule holds only for those of known past' and the king 'not considering' present worth are the proposer's inference, not in either Tamil.

93 the cry and 95 'தேவி தனை விடுவித்த பின்பு' are in plot order; 95 does not name the prince as the one who freed her (a god comes), so 'the prince's help answers the plea' is assumed and teaches is generic.

Both Jain: 1419 'உயிர் பிறிதினில்லை' and 37 'உயிரென்னின் வினை மேலைச் செய்தன்றோ வந்தது'. They agree on the soul's own deed, but 1419 is a brief praise formula that 'not from any other' need not mean 'not from parents', so 'spells out what it denies' is generous.

Both have Kama defeated by beauty, but 706 is the women's thought that Kama has come, 2443 Kama hiding before the bride; that the poem 'sets her beauty above the hero's' is the proposer's inference across different scenes.

1020 the youth burns for the picture, 1035 says the girl 'சென்று சார்ந்தாள்' to the temple at dusk; nothing says she is unanswering or far, so 'his longing has no answer from her yet' is not in the Tamil and it is only sequence.

2357 'முனைவற் றொழுது முடிதுளக்கி' and 2641 'எழின்முடி தீட்டினானே' both show the crowned head bowed; the contrast of whom he bows to is real, but this is a shared image rather than one answering the other.

1339 'பூமியை ஆடற்கொத்த பொறியினன்' is about marks fit to rule the earth, while 1465 reads lotus-marks that make him 'திருமகள் கணவன்' of a merchant's daughter; the rescue also motivates 1339. 'Hidden royalty legible to anyone' overstates and 1465 does not answer 1339.
306 urges giving the girl to Asvagriva, 1146 reports she is wed on earth and he stops his ears; that is plot sequence, and the 'war against the whole discus-lord's host' is not stated in 1146.

2628 says the matrons go in palanquins (சிவிகை ஏறினார்) but not carried by men; 2998 has the gods carry Civakan's palanquin. The shared palanquin is real, but 'men to gods, parting to ascent' is imposed.

627 warns that செருக்கு is the frost that destroys the lotus of wealth; 634 answers with 'என் தோள் உளவாப் பிற பகையினி என் செயும்' as the king smiles, which is the very boast the warning describes, so a claim and the scene that enacts it.

1842 is the spies' report ('என்மரும்') that the elephant moved in one mind with the prince; Kural 599 is about fear of a tiger. The 1833 lion-charge is outside the packet and neither verse shows the elephant won after force, so the pairing is a shared elephant only.

146 the cock cries and falls, 147 the king asks what it is and fears 'பாவம்'; the note is accurate, but the reaction to the preceding event is mostly sequence and 'sign of a sin that binds to births' is the king's reported fear, not doctrine asserted.

2018 says the lamp of காட்சி destroys the darkness of வினை; Tirumanthiram 116 has Nandi remove மும்மலம். A cause-of-release contrast is defensible, but 2018 is silent on any god and 116 has no darkness image, so 'same fire-and-darkness language' and the Tirumanthiram 'gaining the Jain demand' are not in the Tamil.

148 shows Nagadattan hearing dharma and taking the அனசன நோன்பு; the god's birth as reward is not in 148, so the 'limit' the teaches draws is from outside. Kural 345 on the body as excess is a fair partner but the verse only shows the fast.

2265 'அரமங்கையர் சொரிந்தார் மலர்... விசும்பு அடைந்தான்' and Purananuru 287 'மாசில் மகளிர் மன்றல்... உயர்நிலை உலகத்து நுகர்ப' share the warrior's heaven; but the apsaras here shower flowers, not wed, and the challenger is slain in a fair duel, not a man who did not flee, so 'old Puram reward read into the ornament' is generous.
1262 Nilamanikantan laughs at the men; 1270 shows warriors as if the world had no room for them. Irony is plausible but it is story order, and nothing says 1270 are the same men he laughs at.

1977 'மங்கைக் குரியான் கடையேறும் வந்தேறலோடும் வங்கம் நிதியம் உடன் வீழும்' is the astrologers' sign Sagaradattan reports; 1973 'குன்றாமல் விற்றான்' as Civakan sits at the step is its fulfilment, and the note is accurate.

621 shows the goddess of fortune slighted by the king's play in the pond; Kural 617 puts the lotus goddess in the labour of the unslothful (தாளுளான் தாமரையினாள்). Real parallel, and the slighted-lover picture is an addition, but it is only a story of neglect, not a limit on the rule.

Neither poem fixes the Athikan of Akananuru 162 (அதிகன்) as Purananuru 101's Athiyaman Nedumaan Anji; 'of the same house' rests on the name. The line 'நசைபிழைப்பு அறியா' only echoes the idea, so 'epithet of the house' is imposed.

Kural 1075 says fear (அச்சம்) is the conduct of the base; Pazhamozhi 97 says the base do not mind 'பெரும்பழி' and eat unafraid. A contrast is there, but 'held by fear of punishment' is not in the Kural and the proverb is not about blame versus punishment.

440 'கன்னியைத் தருதும்' with the drum, and 479 'ஏழுடன் தருவல்... மணமகனாக' fulfil the proclaimed prize; the one flaw is the note's remark that the chief names himself Govindan, which is not in either verse.

3027 the king puts off jewels and garlands as the world is a drop of milk; Kural 345 speaks of the body being excess. 'First step of a series that reaches the body' is not in the verse, so the pair is an illustration.

595 'தண்ணளி இல்லையேல் உலகு இல்லை' is Marusi's compliment, reported speech of an envoy, near Kural 544's world clinging to the king who embraces his people. The idea is shared, but the verse is flattery and does not extend the couplet.

69 calls the 'ஒற்றை வெண்குடை' the king's finished wealth in the narrator's praise; Siddhar 1790 says desire to rule 'ஓர் குடைக்கீழ்' leaves no way. Different registers, not an incompatible claim, and the Siddhar does not gain a figure he already addresses.

681 'திறைக்கடன்' kindles the fire, 1206 is the envoys' 'புன்சொல்' burning him; 681's anger is not stated to be inward, and the 'second round' at 1207 is outside the packet, so the controlled-to-burning arc is inferred.

3082 'உலகு மூன்றும் விழுங்கியிட்டு' narrates the victory and 3093 'உலகம் மூன்றும் விழுங்கியுமிழாது' repeats it in the worshippers' praise; the Tamil shares the image and the shift from event to creed is true.

Kural 49 allows household life and the ascetic state alike ('அஃதும் பிறன் பழிப்பதில்லாயின் நன்று'), while 66 ends 'துறவறம் பொய் இல்லறமே வாய்' on conditions about the Kali age; both favour the household, but the Kural does not declare renunciation false, so 'agrees' is too tidy.
2607 Vijayai begs the wives 'எங்கும் பிரியற்பீர்' after her dream; 2991 he places them in her care. 'The wish kept in a changed form' is a reading; the second does not answer the first.

628 says one who does not chase pleasure meets no pain; 669 says do the deed that yields joy even through pain. The note itself admits they may differ in scope, which makes them different advice for different situations, not a tension.

708 is the women wondering how the prince who would win her has been caught in the vina's net, which does not clearly name the suitor kings; 798 'நுங்களை வீணை வென்ற' addresses the kings. The 'first round of battle' is inferred.

126 the king names desire (காமம்) as what destroys mind and fame; Siddhar 259 blames a மாயப் பிசாசு in a woman's form. 'Has just spared the woman' is not in 126, so the separation of woman from desire is not shown.
links.text_issue: Siddhar 259 text is cut off at the end ('கச்')

links.reason: 2098 'திருமுடி... தேவர் கொண்டு போய்ப் பாற்கடல் பெய்யப்பட்டதே' and 3035 'படலிகை எடுத்துக்கொண்டு போய்... பாற்கடல் வீழ்ந்ததே' show gods taking the shed token to the milk sea; the hair is not rank as the crown is, but the convention of closing a renunciation is real.

685 'குறிப்பிற் றேறி' has Kattiyankaran read the dancer's signs and then 'செற்றம்' and seizure; Kural 701 praises the one who knows a mind 'குறிப்பறிவான்' as an ornament. The shared word குறிப்பு and the misuse of the skill for a grudge are in the Tamil, and the couplet's good use is a real limit on the case.

2564 'செந்தாமரை மேல் நடந்தான் அடி' and Kural 3 'மலர்மிசை ஏகினான் மாணடி' share the image; that Kural 3's figure is the Jina rests on a reading outside the couplet, and the 'aim of the faithful' clause is already in the couplet's 'சேர்ந்தார்'.

874 shows swords gleaming and the host spreading through the sky (படை... விசும்பிடை நிரந்து); Kural 761 rates a complete army the chief wealth. 'Wealth on show, not strength' is the proposer's reading; the verse neither tests nor denies the army's strength.

140 names the king's single fault, 'கீழ்உயிர் மேல் அருளாமை'; 262 has ministers say that those who bear the 'கீழோர் பிழைத்தன' are followed by the earth. The two are in different councils, and that the poem 'expects counsellors to mend' the fault is not in either.

1757 the parents call the tired girl; 1758 'பந்து கை விட்டு... கழல் சென்று எய்தினாள்' is her coming. It is plot order, and the claim about the swayamvara's choice being left to the father's council is in neither verse.

627 'செருக்கு எனப்படும் திண்பனி' that destroys the lotus of wealth shares the word with Kural 431 'செருக்கும் சினமும் சிறுமையும் இல்லார் பெருக்கம்'; the frost image adds ruin to the couplet's praise, but it is a reported warning and the connection is largely illustration.

47 'பெண்ணுயிர் அளிய... திண்மையும் உடையவல்ல' is the brother's reported thought, answered by the sister that minds fixed on dharma do not love this life; Kural 54 'திண்மை' is கற்பு. The word is shared, but the epic verse does not show a woman standing firm in leaving the world, only an argument that she can.
